why: The single-seed row in production_scale_comparison_2026_10_11 could not separate a real win from a lucky seed. All three full-corpus checkpoints are re-scored under ONE protocol.
protocol: 900 complexes (150 per metal, six metals), non-hydrogen pair scope, BO threshold 0.3, decision=threshold@0.5, per-complex aggregation, seed-0 geometry sample -- identical for all four rows

verdict.bond_EXISTENCE: WIN. 0.9962 +/- 0.0008 vs 0.9771. Margin 0.0191 is 24x the between-seed std.
verdict.macro_F1_over_TYPE: LOSS, consistent across all three seeds. 0.4784 +/- 0.0055 vs 0.5051, i.e. -0.0267 behind. This is the axis the bond head exists to win and it is still lost. Reported, not buried.
verdict.seed_noise_floor_check: All three conclusions survive: existence margin 0.0191 vs std 0.0008; exact-type margin 0.0656 vs std 0.0113; type margin 0.0267 vs std 0.0055. No gap is within seed noise.
verdict.closes_the_withdrawal_loop: The same checkpoints score 0.9398 +/- 0.0269 under the trainer's POOLED gate (cfm_bond_type_f1_3seed.json) and 0.4784 +/- 0.0055 under per-complex aggregation -- nearly a factor of two apart. That is exactly why 0.9194 must never be placed beside OpenBabel's 0.5051.
verdict.what_it_does_NOT_change: macro-F1(type) still loses. Scale helped enormously (n_train 256 gave F1(exist) 0.6118 / type 0.2801 / exact 0.0011) but has not closed the type gap.
